artifact: P-359 CP2 — what was built, what the shipped derivation pass does to the production store read-only, and the re-count against the pre-registered prediction

whatWasBuilt.what: served_geometry jsonb, served_status text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'underived', derivation jsonb, area_published/served double precision, derived_at timestamptz, plus an index on served_status. The default is the fail-closed switch: a row that reaches the table through any path that is not the derivation pass is refused by the reader.

the same columns as drizzle types, plus `EtjServedStatus` (verbatim | derived | repaired | excluded | withheld | underived) and `EtjRingDerivation`. Which statuses are SERVABLE is deliberately NOT declared here: that is the reader's contract and it lives in containment.ts, so there is one list rather than two that can disagree.
the test fixture schema, kept in step with the migration so the integration tests run against the real shape.

the PostGIS derivation/validity pass. One statement: cities (normalized-name -> ST_MakeValid limits), targets (rings for the named published keys), joined (containment of the city's own representative point), shaped (ST_MakeValid, ST_Difference, ST_CollectionExtract), scored (areas in EPSG:3081, the repair delta fraction against the tolerance), verdict (excluded | withheld | derived | repaired | verbatim), then one UPDATE that writes status, served geometry, the two areas, the derivation record and derived_at. The publisher's `geometry` is never assigned to.

after the batch flush, one call to deriveEtjServedGeometry for exactly the city keys just written, in the same function, so nothing leaves the ingest servable only by accident. Rows are inserted with the fail-closed default first.

reports the derivation per publisher: counts by status, and a line per excluded/withheld ring with its note. An operator running an ingest sees the decisions the ingest made about a publisher's drawing.

`EtjBoundaryIndex` {rings, refusals}; `ETJ_SERVABLE_STATUSES` + `statusIsServable` as a type guard; `buildEtjBoundaryIndex` partitions rows (non-servable status, or a servable status with no testable Polygon/MultiPolygon, or no bbox -> a refusal with its reason); `resolveEtjAtPoint` takes the index, and a miss with a refusal in reach is `unresolved`, never `absent`. The refusal is narrowed by the refused ring's published envelope so it can only subtract an answer where the ring could have held the point.
`bboxOfGeometry` accepts `unknown`: the ETJ reader computes an envelope from a row whose geometry it has not accepted yet, and must not assert the thing it is about to check.
EtjFact gains `servedStatus`, `derivationNote` (omitted, not null, when empty) and `refusedRings` [{etjId, servedStatus, reason}].
selects served_geometry / served_status / derivation, builds the reader's index (every candidate row, not only the servable ones), and resolves through it.
exports the new types and functions.

fixtures in both directions, including a real PostGIS container that seeds rings of every class and asserts status, served geometry, recorded areas, idempotency, and that `geometry` is never overwritten.

theGenuineStripStaysTrueFor.whyZeroAbsentIsTheResult: The change had exactly one way to hurt this population — turning a genuine disagreement into a confident absence — and in all six counties it did that to zero parcels. Every strip parcel that moved (763 of 2,162, 35 percent) moved to `unresolved`, and every one of them moved because its own city's ring is one of the 15 excluded rings. `unresolved` is the honest reading there: the published ring is not testable and the reader will not pretend otherwise.

theGenuineStripStaysTrueFor.whatItShows: The genuine strip parcels are NOT moved into `absent`: not one parcel, in any county, becomes a verified absence as a side effect of the refusals. Where a strip parcel does move it moves to `unresolved`. That is the honest decomposition of P-332's 2,160: the population this lane must not touch is not touched in the direction that would matter (a false absence); where it is touched at all it is made honestly unresolved, which is the cost of refusing to serve an unvalidatable ring.

threeQuestionGate.whatExecutes: The derivation: deriveEtjServedGeometry (lib/cad-ingest/src/boundary/etjDerive.ts), called by upsertEtjBoundaries at the end of the ingest for exactly the city keys just written. The validity refusal: buildEtjBoundaryIndex + resolveEtjAtPoint (containment.ts), called by artifacts/api-server/src/lib/etjFactRead.ts on every ETJ determination and by the ingest's own verify instrument. The api-server and the ingest go through the same two functions; there is no second implementation of the rule.
threeQuestionGate.whatTriggers: An ingest run (etjCli.ts / upsertEtjBoundaries) for a publisher, and every ETJ determination on the customer surface. A ring published AFTER this change: the ingest writes it with the column default `underived`, derives it in the same call, and returns — so it is never servable by accident. If the derivation statement itself throws, the ingest call fails and any flushed rows stay `underived`, which the reader refuses and declares; the fail-closed default is what makes that a declaration rather than a silent serve.
threeQuestionGate.whatFails: A ring that reaches the reader as `underived`, `excluded` or `withheld` cannot be tested: it becomes a refusal, and a point that a refusal could have covered is `unresolved` with the refusal's own reason, never `present` and never `absent`. A row that CLAIMS a servable status but carries no testable Polygon/MultiPolygon is refused for that reason instead. The reader cannot re-run ST_IsValid (no PostGIS in the TypeScript path), and it does not pretend to: it trusts `served_status` to mean the pass ran, which is why the column defaults to the one value that means it did not.
threeQuestionGate.whatBypassesIt: (1) A writer that hand-sets both `served_status` and `served_geometry` — a raw INSERT/UPDATE into tx_etj_boundary. Named, not papered over: the default makes the honest path fail closed, but a writer that lies in two columns at once is outside the derivation's reach. (2) A consumer that does not go through buildEtjBoundaryIndex: every LDT reader of tx_etj_boundary was swept (grep over the repo) and they are etjFactRead.ts and containment.ts, both changed; etjVerify.ts reads the live publishers, not the table. (3) Another repo: P-332's close records that hauska-engine's PDF/report path HARDCODES the ETJ value rather than forwarding a read (report-model.ts:966, pdf/feasibility.ts:210-212). That bypass is real, is in another repo, and is reported here rather than claimed fixed.

contradicted.instrumentDefectFoundByMe: The first version of the dry-run generator (gen_dryrun.mjs) — the instrument this lane's re-count leans on — retyped the derivation note by hand instead of extracting it, and after the shipped note grew a branch naming the subtraction beside the repair, the generator went on printing the older sentence. Found by comparing the generator's output against the shipped source rather than by trusting an earlier green run. Fixed: the generator now lifts both the note CASE and the whole derivation jsonb_build_object out of the shipped UPDATE's own text, so the dry run cannot print a sentence the pass does not write. This is the same failure mode P-332 recorded about a per-ring batch that finished, exited 0 and was wrong.
contradicted.p332sRingIds: P-332's close names the three self-containing rings as georgetown-tx:9644, leander-tx:1 and dripping-springs-tx:1. Two of those ids are right; `leander-tx:1` does not exist in tx_etj_boundary (355 rows, 355 distinct ids, verified read-only). The row that actually contains Leander's own city is `leander-tx:7305` (label LEANDER, 211.0 km2, valid, contains its own city). P-332 measured by geometry, not by id, so its counts stand; a reader following the id would have found nothing.
contradicted.p332sInvalidCount: P-332 says 24 of 355 rings are invalid. This lane's read of the same store agrees EXACTLY: the dry run's own identity query prints 355 rings and 24 invalid under ST_IsValid, and the per-ring verdicts sum to the same 24 (1 derived ring whose published geometry is invalid + 8 repaired + 15 excluded). Recorded because this lane first wrote '23' from its own arithmetic (2 derived + 8 + 15 while forgetting that only one of the two derived rings was invalid) and caught it by reading the instrument's own count instead of its own sum. An agreement with P-332 is worth as much in the record as a disagreement.
contradicted.theDispatchsNumber: the dispatch's whatToBuild item 3 predicted the three publishers fall to Georgetown 125 / Leander 111 / Dripping Springs 173. The first two are exactly right; Dripping Springs falls to 0 and the reason is stated above.
contradicted.myOwnTotalsRow: the TOTAL row of this document's own recount table, as first written, said 77,463 / 2,251 and 4 parcels above P-332 on the pre column. The six per-county rows above it sum to 77,462 / 2,250 and P-332's published figure is 77,459, so the correct deltas are 3 and 2. No instrument printed 77,463 or 2,251 — grepping every artifact in P:/tmp/p359-evidence and every file in the scratch directory finds that string only in this draft. The cross-county aggregate queries that could have produced an independent total both died on the read-only compute (recount_a_totals.txt: statement timeout at 900s; recount_c_independent.txt: 'Disk quota exceeded'), so the total was never independently computed and was written by hand. Caught by summing this table's own rows while cross-checking the strip references; corrected here and in the close, and the accounting built on it (3,083 - 173 - 662 + 2 = 2,250) is re-derived from the corrected figures.
